requirements.title: EX descriptor width, digit count, exponent digits, radix restriction, and scale-factor effect
requirements.definition: EX w.d and EX w.d E e occupy w positions except w=0 selects width; d controls hexadecimal fractional digits or selects the minimum exact digit count when zero; d=0 is prohibited unless the internal radix is a power of two; exponent digit count follows descriptor form; e has no input effect; scale factor has no output effect.

pending.EX-field-width: Unassertable as a unique byte-exact finite-output field because the field contents include the p5 processor-dependent exponent/significand choice; IEEE exceptional output can reuse F thresholds under IEEE support.
pending.EX-fractional-hex-digits: Unassertable as a complete finite output oracle without accepting all processor-permitted exponent choices.
pending.EX-d0-minimum-exact-digits: Processor-dependent selected digit count; do not assert a unique output string.
pending.EX-d0-radix-power-of-two-restriction: Context-dependent source-control only: requires knowing the real radix; no diagnostic facet is filed.
pending.EX-exponent-digit-count: Unassertable as one exact finite-output string because EX w.d E e fixes the number of P-exponent digits but not the processor-dependent exponent value; a structural fixture may count digits while accepting all permitted values.
pending.EX-e-no-input-effect: Internal READ('0X1P+2','(EX6.0E2)') and READ('0X1P+2','(EX6.0)') should both approximate 4.0.
pending.EX-scale-factor-no-effect: Unassertable as one exact finite-output string: comparing 1P and 0P EX output must accept all p5 processor-permitted exponent/significand choices, so this source packet supplies no single expected byte sequence.

requirements.oracle: Finite EX output is processor-latitude-sensitive; exact byte plans are deferred unless they test IEEE exceptional forms or accept all allowed exponent choices.

requirements.title: Finite EX output components and processor-dependent binary exponent choice
requirements.definition: Finite EX output has optional sign, 0X, hexadecimal point, significant hexadecimal digits, and a P signed decimal exponent; exponent value choice is processor dependent and may group leading binary digits differently; plus sign is produced for zero exponent.

pending.EX-output-0X-prefix: Unassertable as a unique full output string because the processor chooses the binary exponent/significand grouping; a structural fixture may require 0X after any sign/blanks while accepting all permitted full strings.
pending.EX-output-hexadecimal-point: Unassertable as a unique full output string because the processor chooses the binary exponent/significand grouping; a structural fixture may require one decimal symbol after the first hexadecimal digit.
pending.EX-output-P-exponent: Unassertable as a unique full output string because the processor chooses the binary exponent value; a structural fixture may require a P exponent with sign and decimal digits.
pending.EX-output-binary-exponent-processor-depe: Explicit processor latitude: do not assert whether 1.375 appears as 0X1.6P+0 or another permitted exponent/significand grouping.
pending.EX-output-zero-exponent-plus: Unassertable as a unique full output string unless every permitted processor exponent choice is zero; no such portable finite byte-exact case is asserted in this packet.

requirements.oracle: This requirement is primarily permission/structural because the standard explicitly leaves binary-exponent choice processor dependent.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, three rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_137.json. The reviewer re-derived unit hashes and read Tables 13.1, 13.2 and 13.3 ROW BY ROW against the PDF, independently of the author's reconstruction - necessary because extraction interleaved the columns and every future E/EN/ES fixture derives from those rows. THREE blocking findings. The integrator found the first directly: two sample plans gave a NEGATIVE result for the POSITIVE input 0.5, but SS suppresses the optional plus so the sign position must be BLANK - corrected to ' 500.000E-03' and '   5.000E-01', hand-derived and corroborated with gfortran. C137SR-001: ELEVEN units mixing an obligation with a grant of latitude were dispositioned wholly as permission - the fourth occurrence of that class this session - and were re-dispositioned to requirements with the latitude confined to rationale and oracle text; the reviewer confirmed no latitude is now wrongly asserted as an obligation. C137SR-002: placeholder plans remained, saying things like 'future plan must include exact output'; 48 entries were changed, 21 upgraded to exact executable strings and 27 marked explicitly unassertable, and the reviewer independently derived the scale-factor cases -1P,E10.3E2 giving ' 0.010E+02' and 1P,E10.3E2 giving ' 1.000E+00'. R1323 carries no diagnostic facet because it defines a hex-digit-string form and prohibits nothing. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977.
